finding.claim: Unauthenticated /fetch endpoint passes the user-supplied 'target' query parameter directly to http.Get and returns the response body to the caller, with no allowlist, scheme, port, or redirect validation. Any network client can make the server reach loopback, RFC-1918, cluster-internal services, or cloud metadata and read the response.

trace.note: target read from unauthenticated query parameter on /fetch
passed directly to http.Get with no validation
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) returns the upstream body to the attacker
ListenAndServe(":8080") binds all interfaces, so the endpoint is publicly reachable

finding.guards_checked: None on path: no allowlist or hostname check; no scheme restriction in code (net/http accepts only http/https); no port restriction; redirects followed by default with no CheckRedirect; no authentication; response returned so non-blind. Severity HIGH.

verdict.guard_found: none on the /fetch path. main.go:9-12 defines an allowlist and main.go:27 applies it, but only in safeFetch (main.go:25-38), which is registered at a separate route (main.go:42). fetch (main.go:14-23) passes the query value straight to http.Get at main.go:16 with no check.
verdict.reason: The `target` value is read from an unauthenticated query parameter at main.go:15, passed unvalidated to http.Get at main.go:16, and the upstream body is copied back to the caller at main.go:22, while main.go:43 binds the server to :8080 on all interfaces; the only allowlist (main.go:27) sits in the separate safeFetch handler, so the vulnerable /fetch route has no closing guard.

finding.claim: Allowlisted /safe fetch follows redirects with http.Get and no per-hop re-validation, so a 3xx from an allowlisted host to an internal address (169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1, RFC-1918) is followed and the body returned. Requires an open redirect or compromise on images.example.org or docs.example.org, a trusted-service failure, so downgraded from HIGH to MEDIUM.

trace.note: allowed[u.Hostname()] exact map lookup; err short-circuits so nil u is not dereferenced
http.Get follows up to 10 redirects by default with no CheckRedirect

finding.guards_checked: Exact hostname set membership on .Hostname() (not .Host, not substring) closes direct host injection, including userinfo tricks, case and trailing-dot variants. Allowlist hardcoded at main.go:9-12. No explicit scheme check; non-http(s) schemes fail at transport. Not closed: redirect following without per-hop re-check; DNS rebinding not addressed. Severity MEDIUM.

verdict.guard_found: Exact hostname membership on the parsed host at main.go:27 (`allowed[u.Hostname()]`) closes direct requests to internal hosts. No per-hop redirect validation exists anywhere, so the redirect path is open.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (main.go:26, 27, 31, 37 all match the claim), but the value that would reach an internal address is the Location header from an allowlisted host (main.go:31 follows it), which the remote attacker does not control; the attacker-controlled target at main.go:26 is closed by the exact-match allowlist at main.go:27, so the finding needs a third-party open redirect or compromise, which fails the source check.
